messages:
maria: Follow-up from today's RFC sync: we need a low-friction sampling design for quantization fallbacks that balances signal quality vs cost/latency. goal: detect real regressions quickly without perturbing p95.

diego: Short pitch of possible patterns: (A) synchronous tagging-only sampling (no path change, just mark and store), (B) synchronous reroute to high-precision for a tiny percent, (C) asynchronous shadowing where a copy is run at higher-precision offline, (D) hybrid: tagging + opportunistic shadow for a tiny subset.

helen: ops constraint: any synchronous reroute that hits hotpath will affect tail. so (B) needs extreme caution and very low rates. prefer tagging-only + shadowing.

maria: tagging-only is cheapest in latency terms but gives no ground-truth quality delta unless we shadow. shadowing costs tokens and GPUs. need to quantify token/GPU impact.

vishal: proposal: default to tagging-only at 1% for all traffic. additionally, shadow 0.02% uniformly. on heavy requests (>1024 tokens) bump tagging to 3% and shadow to 0.1% for those. also trigger shadow when internal signals show degraded quant op (e.g., >X early re-rollbacks).

helen: suggested config snippet (informal): {mode: "tag+shadow", tag_rate_pct: 1.0, tag_rate_long_pct: 3.0, shadow_rate_pct: 0.02, shadow_rate_long_pct: 0.1, heavy_token_threshold: 1024, hysteresis_count: 4, max_combined_overhead_pct: 0.5}. We'll formalize later.

diego: telemetry needs: per-sample quality metric (e.g., semantic-similarity delta), token overhead for shadow runs, p50/p95 delta, per-tenant sample counts, and number of hysteresis-triggered upticks. tag traces with quant.sample=true and quant.shadow=true so we can correlate traces.

maria: experiment plan: run baseline control for 1 week with only tagging. then enable shadowing for two weeks with rates above. compare regression rate vs baseline. regression threshold for alarm: >0.75% of sampled requests show quality drop above tolerance.

vishal: fallback escalation policy: if shadow-based detection crosses threshold for a tenant, automatically disable low-bit path for that tenant and create an incident ticket for ML-eng to investigate. need a manual override for enterprise customers.

helen: runtime concerns: adding shadow copies means additional scheduler entries and potential burst GPU allocations. ops will cap total concurrent shadow runs per-region to avoid noisy neighbor. we'll enforce a cross-tenant cap and per-tenant cap.

diego: open design question: should shadow runs use the exact same model weights (but higher precision) or a slightly newer variant? i vote same weights to isolate quantization impact.

maria: agree use identical weights and same prompt context. also ensure deterministic seed where applicable to compare token-by-token diffs when needed.

vishal: metrics names suggested: quant.sample.count, quant.shadow.count, quant.quality.regressions.count, quant.latency.delta.p95, quant.cost.shadow_tokens. tag keys: tenant_id, model, precision_variant.

helen: ops action items: cap settings and runbook for disabling low-bit paths on regression alert (owner: helen).

diego: runtime action items: add flags for tag/shadow rates, heavy thresholds, hysteresis param, and trace labels (owner: diego).

maria: telemetry action items: dashboards and alerts, implement semantic-similarity and token-delta metrics (owner: vishal).

vishal: will also prepare a rough cost estimate for shadowing at proposed rates across regions.

diego: final question: do we allow per-tenant overrides in config? yes/no?

helen: yes — default is system-wide policy but tenants can opt-out or request higher sampling by support ticket; enterprise contracts can pre-specify sampling. we'll add an allowlist/denylist.

maria: good convergence. i'll update the RFC appendix with the chosen hybrid pattern, experiment plan, safety caps, and action owners. closing thread; ping if any blockers. :rocket:
